ui.method.add.standard: Add each column from the right, carrying a 1 over the next column.
ui.method.subtract.standard: Subtract each column from the right, regrouping when the top digit is smaller.
ui.method.divide.standard: Long division: divide, multiply, subtract and bring down, one digit at a time.
ui.method.divide.ladder: Partial quotients: take away friendly groups of the divisor (×100, ×10, ×5 …) down a ladder, then add them up.
ui.method.divide.ladder.1: Pick how many groups of the divisor to take away, like 100, 10, 5 or 2. Write it on the side.
ui.method.divide.ladder.2: Multiply to see how much that is, and write it under what’s left.
ui.method.divide.ladder.3: Subtract. Keep going down the ladder until what’s left is smaller than the divisor.
ui.method.divide.ladder.4: Add the numbers on the side: that’s the quotient. What’s left at the bottom is the remainder.
ui.method.divide.area: Box method: fill sections of a rectangle with the divisor on the side, then add the section widths.
ui.method.divide.area.1: The divisor goes on the side of a rectangle, and the number to divide goes inside.
ui.method.divide.area.2: Pick a width for a section, like 100, 10 or 5, and write it on top. Multiply it by the divisor and take it away.
ui.method.divide.area.3: Start a new section with what’s left, until it’s smaller than the divisor.
ui.method.divide.area.4: Add the widths on top: that’s the quotient. What’s left in the last section is the remainder.
ui.method.multiply.standard: The standard algorithm: multiply each digit, carry, and add the rows.
ui.method.multiply.area: Break both numbers into place-value parts, like (40 + 6) × (20 + 3), fill each box of a rectangle, then add the boxes.
ui.method.multiply.area.1: Break both numbers into their place values: 46 is 40 + 6, and 23 is 20 + 3.
ui.method.multiply.area.2: Each box of the rectangle is one part times another. Multiply to fill it.
ui.method.multiply.area.3: Add all the boxes together: that’s the answer.
ui.method.multiply.partial: List each place-value product down the page (3 × 6, 3 × 40, 20 × 6, 20 × 40), then add the list.
ui.method.multiply.partial.1: Multiply each place of the bottom number by each place of the top number, starting with the ones.
ui.method.multiply.partial.2: Write each product on its own line, lined up on the right.
ui.method.multiply.partial.3: Add all the lines together: that’s the answer.
